notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); gate.digest is the digest the last check printed, and check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package. Recon: the card's entry symbol nidaqmx.task._task:Task was confirmed at generated/nidaqmx/task/_task.py:64, and the package drives one analog input voltage task of that class (the voltage measurement use of examples/analog_in/voltage_sample.py:8-12). DEVIATION FROM THE CARD'S CANDIDATE CLASSES: cap.sensing.read.v1 binds sensor/sensor.imu/sensor.force_torque and cap.actuation.gpio.v1 binds io.gpio/io.digital (catalog show), so neither binds a task that measures a voltage; cap.measure.voltage.v1 is the class that binds the instrument.dmm resource this use corresponds to, and the driver does not bind cap.sensing.read.v1 or cap.actuation.gpio.v1. The card's decision is direct-driver, which the package follows; the helper hint PythonObjectDriver is not used because its fixed command/result map cannot express x-cap.ni.sample_voltages.v1 (two output fields derived from one native read: the list and its length) or the dc precondition of cap.measure.voltage.v1. The card's safety.limit_hints cite enum constants (MAP_RANGES, MAX_SHEAR_STRAIN, MAX_SHEAR_STRAIN_ANGLE) that state no bound, so no Limit comes from them. NOT COVERED: the hardware backend was never opened and no NI-DAQmx runtime is installed or imported (native.py is not imported by any check); the fake is an in-memory stand-in that returns one fixed voltage and one placeholder channel name, not a recording of a device; one waveform-style block read was modelled only as Task.read(count) with an operator-required count (real sample counts, buffer sizing and sample timing are left to the site overlay); the class's optional channel and range_v inputs are not supported because the channel and its range are fixed when the task is created; dc=False (RMS) is refused with MHS.DEVICE.PRECONDITION_UNMET; no cap.device.configure parameter exists because a Task exposes no writable scalar of its own; estop_physical_ref is not set because the card's floor is R1 and no line of the clone documents an independent hardware e-stop. The package is model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json reviewed_by stays null and the hardware backend of a model-authored driver must not run until a human signs it; site-limits.example.json is an example overlay, not a statement about any device.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-10-29; reviewed_by stays null): accepted after a reviewer edit: native.py no longer says that the loader refuses this R1 hardware backend until reviewed_by is signed (the loader refuses only R2 and above).
